context: Your Oct 11 ruling for home: iPhone tests run in GitHub CI only. The shared iOS standard (c91) runs the UI tests once per batch on the Mac through sim-test. Your note, Oct 29 14:46 CDT: some tests belong on CI; too many iOS sessions each start their own simulator and overload your computer; find the balance. Roadmap c196 (cap parallel builds on the Mac) is the step that would set such a cap.

options.gain: CI carries the load; your Mac never runs more than one simulator.
options.how: Unit and UI tests run on GitHub CI for every batch. The Mac runs only a short final check per batch, and only one simulator runs at a time across all repos (the cap from c196).
options.label: CI for the bulk; one short Mac check per batch, one simulator at a time
options.lose: c196's cap must land first; a Mac check waits its turn behind other repos.

options.gain: No simulator load on your Mac at all.
options.how: No session starts a simulator on its own; you run one by hand when you want it.
options.label: All iPhone tests on CI; the Mac only when you ask
options.lose: Nothing checks the app on a simulator per batch.

reply: Picked a, Oct 29 14:55 CDT: CI runs the bulk of home's iPhone tests; one short Mac check per batch, one simulator at a time across repos once c196's cap lands.
title: home: where do the iPhone tests run, GitHub CI or the Mac?
why: It keeps a per-batch check while capping what runs on your Mac at one simulator.
